researcher_notes:
Scope note: per task instructions, Coates Group was already fully researched in the Drive-Thru/Voice AI batch (3 records: McDonald's ANZ x2, Hungry Jack's) and was skipped entirely here. This batch covers only Mood Media and Rise Vision. No usable raw material existed in restaurant_tech_research_2026-07-21.json's candidate_evidence (936 rows) or verified_seed_evidence (38 rows) arrays for either vendor -- searched for 'mood media', 'risevision'/'rise vision', 'digital menu board', and 'digital signage' as substrings across all rows and got zero hits -- so all records below came from fresh web research against each vendor's own case-study pages.

Mood Media (6 records): Mood Media's own site hosts a substantial restaurant/QSR case-study library, but most of the big-name entries (Wendy's, Burger King, Moe's, Caribou Coffee, Jamba, T-Bones Great American Eatery) turned out on inspection to document Mood's MUSIC/audio business, not digital menu boards or visual signage -- Burger King's case study mentions unspecified 'video screens' playing music-video content in Hungarian locations but does not describe menu-board or merchandising signage, so it was excluded as off-category rather than force-fit. The 6 records kept here are the ones where the case study explicitly documents a visual digital-signage/menu-board deployment: Fryday (Romania, 11-unit fast-food chain, deployment described as installed 'across all restaurants'), McDonald's via Premier Restaurants Romania (the Romanian developmental licensee, 100+ locations/29 cities, full digital signage ecosystem including menu boards), Wagamama (3 named UK airport locations with detailed LED/menu-board specs), Louisiana Famous Fried Chicken, Dominic's Casual Italian, and Stash's Pizza (three smaller/regional case studies, all undated on-page but referencing the December 2016 FDA menu-labeling deadline as context). None of Mood's own case-study pages carry an explicit publish date; where a PDF filename path implied a WordPress upload date that was used as an approximate proxy and flagged as such in that record's notes, otherwise source_date is 'undated'.

Rise Vision (2 records): thin. Rise Vision's own restaurant industry page displays a wall of restaurant-brand customer logos (Pizza Guys, Dallas BBQ, Ritual, Whistle Stop Ice Cream, Village Tavern, Cunningham Restaurant Group, City BBQ, WowBao, Pepper Lunch, De Leon Foods) but none of these have a dedicated case study, quote, date, or disclosed deployment scope behind them -- logo-only marketing placement, not usable as sourced evidence, so no records were created for them. Only two named restaurant accounts have an actual dated case-study writeup with specifics: Famous Famiglia (deployed via reseller/integrator HD2Menus.com at Houston Bush Intercontinental and Sacramento International airport locations, published 2015-11-17) and Kamado Grille (a single independent restaurant in Raleigh, NC, deployed via integrator No Static AV, published 2015-06-22). IMPORTANT CAUGHT ERROR: an early web-search summary claimed Rise Vision had 'McDonald's and Starbucks case studies' -- this was verified false by fetching the actual source article (risevision.com/blog/5-ways-how-digital-signage-improves-qsrs): that post cites generic third-party industry statistics about McDonald's, Starbucks, Pizza Hut and Burger King's OWN digital signage programs (i.e. industry benchmarking commentary), not claims that any of those brands are Rise Vision customers. No records were created for those brands.

Corporate-structure finding -- Mood Media: was Nasdaq/TSX-listed as Mood Media Corp; filed a voluntary prepackaged Chapter 11 reorganization in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court (S.D. Texas) in 2020 that cut debt by roughly $404M; emerged from Chapter 11 and was then acquired by private equity firm Vector Capital, with that acquisition completing 2021-01-07. Mood Media is therefore now a privately-held company under Vector Capital ownership, not publicly traded -- vendor_ticker is set to null throughout. It is still operating under the 'Mood Media' name (not defunct or renamed), so it is not placed in the defunct/renamed flag list below, but the ownership change is material context for account intelligence. Rise Vision: no evidence of any acquisition, merger, or renaming was found; it appears to remain an independent, privately-held Canadian company (Rise Vision Inc.) focused primarily on the education/corporate-communications market, with restaurants as a smaller secondary vertical -- consistent with the task brief's framing.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor-published case study (not independent trade press) but highly specific: names the brand, country, unit count ('as of Q2 2024, 11 restaurants'), exact solution list (digital menu boards, video walls, drive-thru menu boards, info points, price lists, junior-meal screen), '100+ Harmony video players installed across all restaurants', and an on-record CEO quote (Lucian Florea). Explicit 'across all restaurants' language supports all_location_deployment for this specific 11-unit chain.
records.notes: Fryday is an 11-unit Romanian fast-food chain (peanut-oil-fried food, smashed Romanian Angus beef burgers), not a globally recognized brand -- included because the deployment evidence is unusually specific and complete for a digital-menu-board record. Deployment also included drive-thru menu boards and video walls, i.e. broader than menu boards alone. 'As of Q2 2024' is the only concrete date anchor in the source content itself and is used as source_date; the case-study page carries no separate publish-date byline. Also available via Mood Media's UK/international mirror site (moodmedia.com/gb/case-studies/fryday/) with matching content.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor-published case study naming the specific licensee (Premier Restaurants Romania), exact scope ('over 100 restaurants... across 29 Romanian cities, including drive-thrus and McCafes'), and a detailed solution list (digital menu boards, video walls, digital price lists, info kiosks, touchscreens/tablets, single screens) with a direct quote describing Mood as designing, installing, and configuring 'the full digital signage ecosystem'. Corroborated independently via Romania-Insider and Premier Capital trade coverage of Premier Restaurants' McDonald's franchise operations in Romania (confirms Premier Restaurants Romania is McDonald's developmental licensee for the country), though those articles do not themselves mention Mood Media.
records.notes: brand recorded as 'McDonald's' per naming rule -- the actual contracting entity is Premier Restaurants Romania, McDonald's developmental licensee/franchisee for Romania (a separate legal operator, not McDonald's Corporation directly), and the deployment scope is that licensee's own restaurant footprint (100+ locations, 29 cities), not a McDonald's global or US brand-standard program. Case study states Premier Restaurants was 'already a loyal music client' before expanding to the full digital-signage buildout. No explicit publish date on the case study page; also mirrored on Mood Media's Ireland site (moodmedia.com/ie/case-studies/mcdonalds/) with identical content, and referenced in a 2026 Mood Media EMEA LinkedIn post, but neither gives a firm original publish date.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor case study with unusually precise technical detail (6.25mm pixel-pitch LED, a 21m x 2m / 68-cabinet seamless installation at Heathrow T5, day-parted content scheduling), which is a strong signal of an authentic, non-generic writeup, but it is still vendor-self-published rather than independent press, and scope is explicitly limited to 3 named airport units, not the full UK/global Wagamama estate.
records.notes: Deployment is airport-only: London Gatwick, London Heathrow Terminal 5, and London Heathrow Terminal 3 -- three named restaurant locations, each with digital menu boards plus large-format LED video walls (Terminal 5 install described as a single seamless LED wall). No claim made or implied about Wagamama's non-airport estate.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor case study with a specific, named regional chain, explicit multi-state footprint, and a concrete solution description (4 dynamic screens, multi-zone layout) -- but it is vendor-self-published with no independent corroboration and no confirmed publish date.
records.notes: Regional QSR chain with locations in Texas, Arizona, California, and Michigan; case study describes 4 dynamic-screen digital menu boards used for menu content, seasonal promotions, and compliance with the FDA menu-labeling rule that took effect 2016-12-01 (that date is case-study CONTEXT, not the deployment or publish date). source_date of 2019-08 is inferred only from a downloadable PDF version of this same case study hosted at a WordPress media path stamped '/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/...' -- treat as an approximate upload/publish proxy, not a confirmed date. Also mirrored on Mood Media UK, Russia, and GCC regional sites with matching content.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor case study naming a small independent 2-location restaurant group with a specific, credible deployment description (3 static screens, multi-zone layout) -- low stakes/low ambiguity content, but vendor-self-published and undated.
records.notes: Very small chain: 2 locations (Gladstone, MO -- pickup/drive-thru; Kansas City, MO -- sit-down dining). Case study references the FDA menu-labeling deadline of 2016-12-01 as context for why the digital board's quick-edit capability mattered, but does not give an actual implementation or publish date.

records.confidence_rationale: Vendor case study confirms a real deployment (six-screen static digital menu board per location, multi-zone layout) but does not disclose how many locations 'multi-location pizzeria' actually means, and is undated.
records.notes: Described only as a 'multi-location pizzeria serving the Boston, MA area' -- exact unit count not given. Same FDA 2016-12-01 menu-labeling context referenced as in the Dominic's and LA Fried Chicken case studies, suggesting these three may be from the same content batch, but this is inference, not stated fact.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated (2015-11-17), named brand, named specific airport terminals with exact media-player counts per location, on-record quotes from both the restaurant operations manager and the deploying integrator's owner, and a clear technical description of Rise Vision's role (software platform running on Google Chrome OS hardware) versus the integrator's role (HD2Menus.com, design/install).
records.notes: Rise Vision was the underlying digital-signage software platform; HD2Menus.com was the reseller/systems integrator that designed, sold, and installed the solution. Deployment: George Bush Intercontinental Airport, Houston TX -- 3 terminal locations (Terminal E x2, Terminal B x1) totaling 13 media players -- plus a stated additional deployment at Sacramento International Airport (player count not given for that location). Airport/travel-retail locations specifically, not confirmed for Famous Famiglia's non-airport footprint.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated (2015-06-22), named single-location restaurant, specific hardware/software stack described (Mac Minis running Rise Vision software driving 2 LED video walls plus bar-area displays, live kitchen camera feeds), and named integrator (No Static AV) with a quote. Confidence held to Medium rather than High because this is one independent restaurant, not a multi-unit brand, and content leans toward general entertainment/ambiance display more than menu-board merchandising specifically.
records.notes: Kamado Grille is a single independent restaurant in Raleigh, NC -- not a multi-unit chain -- so 'all_location_deployment' here means the deployment covers the brand's one disclosed location, not evidence of chain-wide scale. Content mix is broader in-store display (video walls, live kitchen feed, promotions, quizzes) rather than a pure menu board, which is why this still fits the category but was not scored higher than Medium confidence for menu-board specificity. Integrator No Static AV (Burbank, CA) supplied and installed the AV hardware; Rise Vision supplied the software running on Mac Mini players.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Rise Vision -- restaurant industry page lists ~10 additional restaurant-brand customer logos (Pizza Guys, Dallas BBQ, Ritual, Whistle Stop Ice Cream, Village Tavern, Cunningham Restaurant Group, City BBQ, WowBao, Pepper Lunch, De Leon Foods) with no dedicated case study, quote, date, or disclosed deployment scope behind any of them -- logo-wall marketing only, not usable as sourced evidence, so no records were created for these.
